source_scope: Pettersson1999 printed101–108, directly visually inspected. Nine analytical expressions are taken from prior checked ledger; actual sign values remain unknown.

claims.observation: Within the selected nine proposed expressions, i and u counts do not exceed7; tilted t groups occur as4t in three cases.
Author motivates i/t=8 by interpreting4t as half an i.
claims.missing_anchor: No independent statement that4t equals half an i; regular four-stroke group could have another value or function.

claims.observation: Author explicitly considers4t a nonnumerical mark and i,t as different categories.
claims.scope: Countermodels test numerical hypotheses without excluding a nonnumerical category.

claims.observation: Paper distinguishes metal-tool subset from wider corpus and weighs arguments against weight notation.
claims.scope: A countermodel to uniqueness of a base is not a positive reading or whole-script theory.

hypotheses.canonical_integer_carrying: Ordered denominations t<i<u<x with integer ratios >=2; each lower count is less than its adjacent ratio. Highest x may repeat without an assumed higher unit. This is an added convention.
hypotheses.unrestricted_addition: Arbitrary positive values allow any finite count expression; addition alone does not imply a base.
hypotheses.half_equation: 4t=i/2 fixes i/t=8 only if this equality is an externally justified premise.
hypotheses.uniform_ratio: A common ratio across all adjacent denominations is another premise; mixed ratios remain possible.

exclusions: No gram values are assigned in abstract countermodels.
No ordering, phonetic or semantic reading is established.
No independent uniform sampling of quantities assumed; no p-value for missing8/9digits.
The tool expressions remain disputed. All nine source rows and two K121 alternatives are included, not claimed primary verified on nine artifacts.
